findings.description: Critical: DispatchExecutionContext requires worktree_root, but the plan never specifies who resolves and attaches that canonical root. dg-06 RoutingDispatchContext has no worktree_root field, and autopilot PhaseDispatchPayload only carries isolation (no root, no decision_id). Design D1 says routed callers merely copy the dg-06 assignment, which cannot populate the required root, so implementers cannot build a valid execution context for routed, standalone, or local-provider launches.
findings.resolution: Specify the producer of worktree_root for each caller (router/orchestrator, review adapter, autopilot local provider), extend PhaseDispatchPayload or an adjacent carriage field as needed, and document validation against git rev-parse --show-toplevel plus the existing managed-worktree/shared-checkout rules before sandbox preparation.

findings.description: Critical: Design D5 only says the child environment strips proxy variables, but SRT 0.0.77 skips its resolved-address/domain allowlist checks for connections routed through parentProxy, including HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY inherited by the srt process itself. If implementers strip proxies only for the vendor argv after SRT starts, or leave ambient proxies on the env passed to absolute_srt, authored network policy can be bypassed while still reporting applied=true.
findings.resolution: Require that the environment passed to the SRT executable itself excludes HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, http_proxy, https_proxy, all_proxy, and related parentProxy inputs unless an explicitly approved chaining mode is defined; add a RED test that ambient proxy env cannot widen egress under an allowlisted settings file.
findings.existing_code:
The child environment removes inherited proxy variables, loader/startup injection variables,
Git path/config overrides, and untrusted temp settings that can alter SRT or its child.

findings.description: Critical: Tasks 5.1-5.2 require a controlled vendor fixture and a real capable-host SRT probe with persisted evidence, and design/roadmap acceptance require observable FS/network restriction plus recorded capable-host proof. wp-validation-docs write_allow is only docs/** and openspec trees, so fixture/probe code cannot be landed there, and its verification step only runs openspec validate — a green package does not prove the dg-07 acceptance outcomes.
findings.resolution: Move 5.1-5.2 implementation into wp-runtime/wp-integration write scopes (or widen wp-validation-docs write_allow accordingly), and add a verification/evidence gate that either records a capable-host pass artifact or fails closed with the exact missing prerequisites rather than treating openspec validate as sufficient.

findings.description: Nit: wp-policy-audit and wp-runtime are parallel (both depends_on: []) yet both include openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/** in write_allow. Parallel packages therefore have overlapping mutable scope for tasks.md/contracts/specs, which the work-package validity rules disallow and which will race during coordinated implementation.
findings.resolution: Remove the shared openspec write_allow from one or both parallel packages, or serialize them; keep OpenSpec checkbox/doc updates in a single non-parallel package.

findings.description: Nit: Fail-open durability depends on a mode-0600 local outbox with fsync and later drain, but proposal/design/specs never define the outbox directory, filename scheme, ownership, retention, or crash recovery. Without a fixed path outside the mutable worktree and world-writable temp races, the durable-before-fallback guarantee is not implementable consistently across hosts.
findings.resolution: Pin an absolute outbox location (for example under XDG_STATE_HOME/agentic-coding-tools/sandbox-outbox), directory mode 0700, file mode 0600, atomic append+fsync semantics, and drain ordering; add tests for coordinator-down then later drain.
findings.existing_code:
The backend first writes a durable coordinator event; if unavailable,
it appends and fsyncs a mode-0600 local outbox. Failure of both blocks dispatch.

findings.description: Nit: Sandbox audit SHALL not acknowledge durable success until the audit row is inserted, but the existing AuditService.log_operation path returns success=True under async_logging before the insert runs. The plan says synchronous durable audit in tasks 2.4 without explicitly forbidding reuse of that fire-and-forget API, so implementers can satisfy the task text while violating the durable-before-fallback scenario.
findings.resolution: Specify a dedicated synchronous sandbox-event persistence path that awaits/commits the row (or equivalent durable store) before ack; explicitly ban AuditService async fire-and-forget for applied=false fail-open gating.
findings.existing_code:
if config.audit.async_logging:
            # Fire-and-forget: don't block the caller. `success=True` here means
            # "accepted for writing", not "written" — the insert has not run yet.
            task = asyncio.create_task(self._insert_audit_entry(data))
            self._pending.add(task)
            task.add_done_callback(self._pending.discard)
            return AuditResult(success=True)

findings.description: Nit: vendor-dispatch and design D8 require cancellation to pass through the shared process backend, but CliVendorAdapter has no cancel subprocess sink today — cancelled appears only as an async envelope state observed by poll. The plan therefore over-claims a lifecycle command that does not exist, which will confuse AST-guard and RED/GREEN coverage for cancel.
findings.resolution: Either narrow the requirement/scenarios to sync, async submit, and poll (with cancelled as a polled terminal state), or add an explicit cancel command path and tests before claiming backend ownership of cancel.
findings.existing_code:
includes synchronous execution, asynchronous submission, asynchronous polling/cancellation, and
the autopilot local-provider harness.

findings.description: Nit: DispatchExecutionContext allows decision_id null for every source, including source=router, while the routed-execution scenario requires the same decision identifier to appear in execution audit and dg-06 contexts require a non-empty decision_id. The schema therefore admits router-sourced contexts that cannot satisfy the immutability acceptance scenario.
findings.resolution: Add a schema constraint or explicit validation rule: when source is router, decision_id MUST be a non-empty string; keep null only for agents_yaml/default standalone fallback.

findings.description: Nit: The agent-coordinator sandbox-event requirement says events SHALL include routing correlation, requested/applied isolation, runtime/preflight outcome, policy revision/digest, canonical root, executable paths, environment key names, and degradation reason, but sandbox-execution-event.schema.json leaves decision_id, preflight_status, policy_revision, policy_digest, worktree_root, executable_paths, and degradation_reason optional. Producers can emit schema-valid events that fail the SHALL clause and weaken fail-open observability.
findings.resolution: Make the SHALL fields required for sandbox execution events (or define a discriminated applied=true/false subset where each required field is mandatory), and align tests to reject sparse degraded events.

findings.description: Nit: Design D3 rejects roots that are the shared checkout, but does not bind that check to the already-landed skills/shared/checkout_policy.py managed-worktree detector (.git-worktrees/...). Leaving shared-checkout detection unspecified invites a second, divergent heuristic and false accepts/rejects for linked worktrees versus the primary checkout.
findings.resolution: Require sandbox root validation to reuse classify_checkout/_managed_worktree_root (or an extracted pure helper) so managed linked worktrees are accepted and the shared checkout is rejected consistently.
findings.existing_code:
The root must exist, equal `git rev-parse
--show-toplevel`, and must not be `/`, the user's home, or the shared checkout.

findings.description: Optional: network-policy-export.schema.json accepts optional ports via [1-9][0-9]{0,4}, which allows values above 65535 (for example 99999). SRT port suffixes are real TCP ports; invalid ports can either fail closed late or be dropped inconsistently during rendering.
findings.resolution: Tighten the port portion to 1-65535 (and add a unit test for 65536 rejected).

findings.description: FYI: Coordinator SQL matching in is_domain_allowed replaces '*' with SQL LIKE '%' (multi-label), while exported patterns are enforced under SRT wildcard semantics. Operators may see advisory check_domain and sandboxed egress disagree for the same authored pattern; the plan covers deny-first narrowing but not this wildcard-depth mismatch.
findings.resolution: Document that export/SRT is authoritative for sandbox enforcement, and add a renderer/export note or normalization test if LIKE-depth equivalence is desired later.
findings.existing_code:
AND (
              p_domain = np.domain_pattern
              OR p_domain LIKE REPLACE(np.domain_pattern, '*', '%')

findings.description: Post-SRT-start failures correctly fail closed with no unsandboxed retry, and missing/incompatible runtime fail-open only after durable audit/outbox evidence. That closes the double-execution hazard called out in the proposal and matches the Runtime failure never duplicates work scenario.
findings.resolution: Retain this invariant through implementation review; do not add unsandboxed retry paths in timeout or nonzero-exit handling.
findings.existing_code:
WHEN SRT has started and exits nonzero or times out
THEN the backend SHALL return that failure
AND SHALL NOT retry the vendor command without the sandbox.

findings.description: The plan pins @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime 0.0.77 with lockfile integrity, forbids dispatch-time install, rejects pre-0.0.16 network-escape versions, and requires a no-op launch preflight before applied=true. That is the right dependency posture for a pre-1.0 enforcement backend.
findings.resolution: Keep the pin/preflight tests as merge gates; do not relax to PATH-discovered unmarked srt binaries.
